result:
I couldn't run the tests, because pytest isn't installed in this environment.

The bug was in `strip_reminders` in `anthrouter/request_text.py`. Its docstring promises to "trim outer whitespace", but it never did. After removing the `<system-reminder>` block, the newline that followed it stayed at the start of the text. `is_activity_label_prompt` does a `startswith` check, so the leading `\n` made it return `False`.

I fixed it in `strip_reminders` itself, which now ends with `.strip()`. That also fixes any other caller that relies on a reminder-stripped string, including local-command matching and the router's classifier input, not just the activity-label check.

I haven't checked whether any existing test expects the old untrimmed output from `strip_reminders`, so run `make test` before relying on this.
